analysis.title: Systematic Sampling: The Transect
analysis.description: An instructional slide explaining transect sampling in ecological studies, featuring a title and explanatory paragraph at the top, and an illustrative diagram across the bottom depicting a measuring tape transect line running from dense woodland to open grassland with quadrats positioned at regular intervals.
analysis.layout: The slide is laid out vertically with text occupying the upper half (centred title followed by left-aligned explanatory text block) and a panoramic illustration occupying the lower half, showing a gradient transition from forest to meadow with a horizontal tape measure and glowing square quadrat samples.

components.visibleText: A transect is a straight line drawn across a habitat where conditions are changing. We place quadrats at regular intervals (e.g., every 2 metres) along this line to track changes systematically.
